cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've released the gallery from hosting my exhibition. They need room for smaller ambitions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected us. Shall I collect your paintings?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yes. Withdrawing my best work gives them space to recover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already put it outside. I'll bring the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'm conceding the pavement too. No need to overshadow their entrance.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 presents rejection as releasing the gallery, A3 approves removal as giving recovery space and A5 grants the pavement as another concession, maintaining superiority throughout retreat.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 rejection correction and retrieval offer cause A3 withdrawal claim; B4 paintings already outside cause A5 pavement concession and van approval.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 focus on collecting exposed artwork, supplying practical help despite A self-protective rhetoric.

heightening.evidence: B4 outside placement strips A claim to interior control, causing A5 to claim deliberate control of the remaining pavement space.

specificity.evidence: A1 exhibition and B2 rejected paintings establish the loss; B4 van is a plausible offered retrieval tool.
